content:
alice (Support): Heads up — escalated ticket from AcmeCorp. They downgraded mid-cycle (Pro -> Standard) on 2025-09-08 but were invoiced for full month. Paid with PO PO-9987 (VAT reverse-charge flagged). They want a partial credit note for the unused days. Invoice INV-2025-342 attached in the Zendesk thread.
sam (CS): Thanks. Can you paste invoice lines + billing period and the exact downgrade timestamp? Need to repro on our side before issuing a note.
alice (Support): Billing period: 2025-09-01 -> 2025-09-30. Downgrade event recorded 2025-09-08T14:12:22Z. Invoice total: 9,000 EUR (incl. VAT 20% on configurable lines). Pro plan monthly price = 9,000 EUR (VAT incl).
jordan (Billing): Quick question — was the PO processed as tax-exempt because of the reverse-charge? That affects calculation: if invoice recorded net vs gross we might be double-counting VAT when computing credit.
alice (Support): PO metadata shows reverse_charge=true and customer VAT id present. They expected net pricing, but invoice shows VAT line present.
maria (Finance): I'm pulling ledger now. Initial observation: ledger has full-month posted charge on 2025-09-01, and a prorate credit attempt on 2025-09-09 that failed reconciliation. The attempted credit amount in ledger = -6,612 EUR, but expected ~-6,000 EUR (net basis).
jordan (Billing): Repro steps I used: 1) fetch invoice line net_price = round(gross / (1+vat)) 2) compute unused_days = days_between(downgrade_date, period_end) 3) prorated_net = net_price * (unused_days/total_days) 4) credit_gross = round(prorated_net * (1+vat))
Example with numbers:```
# params
gross_month = 9000.00
vat = 0.20
total_days = 30
unused_days = 22  # 9/9 through 9/30 inclusive => 22 days

net_month = gross_month / (1 + vat)  # = 7500.00
prorated_net = net_month * (unused_days / total_days)  # = 7500 * 22/30 = 5500.00
credit_gross = round(prorated_net * (1 + vat), 2)  # = 6600.00
```
So I'd expect credit_gross ~ 6,600 EUR. Why did ledger show -6,612? Could be rounding on per-token (per-seat) lines or timezone causing unused_days=21.9 => rounding up.
maria (Finance): Ledger shows we used unused_days=21 in that attempt (we computed from 09-09 00:00 local instead of 09-08T14:12Z). That yields prorated_net = 5250 => credit_gross = 6300. So that doesn't match either. Looking deeper: there was also a platform discount proration applied (pro-rated discount of 12 EUR) and the system applied VAT on the discount differently, yielding -6,612.
alice (Support): So two problems: (1) we mis-calculated days because of timezone/truncation; (2) discount led to an edge-case VAT rounding delta. Customer sees higher credit expectation than ledger. They want a formal credit note and explanation.
jordan (Billing): Proposed remediation: issue a manual credit note that equals the customer-visible expected amount (6,600 EUR) and tag it with original invoice INV-2025-342 and PO-9987. For accounting: post offset entry to correct the rounding/different VAT handling, then file a reconciliation run for the month.
maria (Finance): I agree with manual credit but we must preserve tax compliance: because PO is reverse-charge, the credit should mirror tax treatment. On the credit note lines set VAT=0 and add a note: "Reverse-charge — customer VAT ID xx-999 applied on original invoice". Also include a ledger memo referencing the algorithmic discrepancy.
billing-bot: Credit note draft CN-2025-77 created by maria — amount 6600.00 EUR, status=draft.
sam (CS): Can we confirm that refund/payment will not attempt to refund external payment method? This must be a credit note (accounting credit) since they paid via PO/transfer. Customer asked for a refund to card? They explicitly said credit against next invoice.
maria (Finance): Confirmed — credit note only (no refund to card). We'll create a memo and set apply_to_next_invoice=true.
jordan (Billing): I'll open a small patch to proration logic to: 1) compute unused_days using UTC timestamp boundaries, 2) always compute proration on net-first (strip VAT), 3) apply discounts at the net level before VAT, and 4) add deterministic rounding to 2 decimal places at line-level. That will avoid the 12 EUR drift.
alice (Support): Can you also include a reproducible test case in the PR? Include the exact payload we get from billing webhook (invoice lines, discounts, vat flags) so we can replay for customer.
jordan (Billing): Yep. Test case created in repo: billing/proration/tests/test_acmecorp_mid_cycle.py — includes the downgrade timestamp, PO metadata, and expected CN value.
billing-bot: PR #2483 opened by jordan: "fix(proration): deterministic net-first proration + timezone fix".
maria (Finance): I've moved CN-2025-77 from draft -> issued. Posted ledger adjustment to offset the earlier incorrect credit attempt. Accounting entries: AR decrease 6600 EUR, VAT reverse-charge note attached.
alice (Support): Verified with AcmeCorp — they received credit note CN-2025-77 and accepted. Marking ticket as resolved. Thanks team :white_check_mark: 
sam (CS): Nice. Can we run a backfill to find other customers affected by the same rounding bug in Sep 2025?
maria (Finance): I'll run a query for all proration credits between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 where difference between expected_gross and posted_gross >= 5 EUR. Will report back.
